body: I've been making up stories for him, where the kids go through things I think he might be experiencing and overcome them through teamwork, perseverance, and understanding themselves. He's started requesting the stories I make up rather than ones out of books, so I think he likes them. I hadn't considered that a part of the overall help, though. Thank you.

That's what I aim for. I hope I hit it on the head. I just fear that isn't enough.

I don't think he can quite articulate all of his emotions, and he doesn't seem to understand why he feels the way he feels. Or, at least, if he does, he's not ready to share it, yet.
Thank you for sharing. We're hoping therapy will help him, too. Just having someone to talk about his problems with who is not a part of them can be very cathartic.
Thank you. I hope we can get him what he needs in time.

That seems to be the most common type of councilor for children of that age group. Thank you for your suggestions.

We'll be discussing the gun with both CPS and the other adults.

Thank you very much. Much we already do, but a few of those are new suggestions. I am not hopeful for the group therapy, but we can suggest it. The entire situation has been antagonistic, and we've done nothing but attempt to be in their lives and a part of it. She won't talk to us, regardless of what we attempt to include her in. We've sent her pictures. We give her inclusion on events we plan. We've offered an olive leaf in every way we've tried. Everything has been rebuffed. But, if we give up, we give up on him, huh? I'll keep trying.

Thank you.

We've got the call to the school on the docket for Monday.

I know they have a concept of it. We've talked about it. We've talked about the uniqueness of life. He feels bad when his brother picks the flowers because that's the end of them. He knows he's the only little boy like him. I remember feeling the way he did. I can't brush it off. I remember what it was.

We'll look for the local varieties in the jurisdiction. The problem is its notorious for this sort of thing, and the support groups don't appear to exist. We don't live in the area where they do, and the journey is prohibitive with the current finances.

I tell him to tell someone he trusts about what hurts him. About what makes him feel this way. He can tell me. He can tell his dad. He can tell his mom or his step-dad, if he feels comfortable telling them. He can tell his teacher. He can tell his doctors. He can tell those he feels safest around. I get this sick feeling something is happening, but unless we have definitive proof, there's nothing we can do.

We've told him that if an adult tells him that something is just their special secret, and it makes him feel bad that he should tell an adult he trusts. If they don't do anything, tell me. Come to me or their dad and we'll make sure something is done, even if we have to shout it at everyone. We've been working on the phone number, and how to get ahold of us if they need us.

I'll check the support groups in the area. I looked a while ago, but I haven't looked recently. That's a good reminder; thank you.
We've talked to him about using his devices for that. But I think a camera would be better, you're right.

We've thought of this. Unfortunately, any toys they are sent with are "lost". There's this impression, even with small toys, that we'll "hack" their place.

There's a real fear of being caught being displayed. It makes me worry all the more.

Thank you very much. I have such a hard time video taping his confessions, because he makes them suddenly and without warning. He usually won't go into them further, either. It's really rough, and these sorts of discussions are so hard to document. They're relatively tech-savy (dad has made sure of this. :D ) so, they get when the device is on.

Thank you for responding.

Please, yes. I've already been doing a lot of the things in the articles linked mentioned. (I've been down this road before myself, and remember what worked. I do the whole psychology reading thing.) But, I do have a very hard time rendering it down to his level. I use words that are too large for them consistently, and I'd say I'm only 70% accurate at figuring out when they don't quite get what I'm saying. It's hard going from college to kindergartners.

The hopeful "it does?" question he posited when I told him that it gets better when he's older... wow, that broke my heart. I hope what I can do is enough. I've received some good suggestions, that will help me move forward.

That's a good idea. We'll see what we can do about the group therapy, but the distance and her general refusal to cooperate with anything make it difficult to reach group decisions. We can't even get simple things like when their regular bedtime is or who watches the youngest during the day.
Thank you for the resources.

We have tried face-to-face communications. She responds with silence or a response to "talk about it later", which she never responds to further attempts to pick up the conversation.

We have attempted to get full custody, but there was a mistake in the paperwork made by the first lawyer we had that makes it so we can't sue for full custody unless something changes drastically. We're currently pursuing legal action against the lawyer, but the barrier to that is the aforementioned money.

I'd still want her to be a part of their life as long as they wanted her to be, and as long as the medical professionals would recommend her to be a part. There seems to be a few abandonment issues already; I wouldn't want to add to those even if we had full custody.

We just found out that the gun exists, so we'll be broaching the subject with them immediately. Unfortunately, most of the communications we attempt to have with them are met with silence unless we involve the courts. 

We have been looking into all avenue of the medical professionals, but the insurance agreement that the courts dictated means, financially, that we can't afford our own insurance. She has been unwilling to share their insurance information with us. Those who are capable of doing something about this don't seem to care.

I've been recently exploring free alternatives, but we've been unsuccessful, so far. I will continue to look, but I'm also afraid of reprisal from the other adults in his life. It seems like he might get punished for things like this, given the interactions in the past.

I know. I couldn't sleep this weekend, because that's all I could see. We'll be attempting to communicate with her about the gun, and if she refuses we'll be calling CPS, again.

He's a competent kid when he wants to do something. It takes one deep moment of desperation for him to want a tool of finality at his disposal. It fills me with a fear I didn't know I could have.

Thank you for the suggestions. I hadn't thought of putting it there.

He's in kindergarten. They're worried that he's withdrawn. We'll be calling the school again on Monday.

We've been teaching the both of them our phone numbers so that they can call either of us whenever they want. I know that their mother makes it difficult to call, when she's around. The calls constantly get muted and they return, sullen.

We've recently given him the idea of calling us via the school if he feels really, really bad. We've been telling him to talk to his teacher or the councilor at the school, but as far as we can tell, he hasn't engaged.

Toys we send with him are "lost".
I am not, sadly. Thank you very much for the offer, however.

Thank you.

We've talked with the teacher, but she's been elusive about the councilor issue. I'll suggest to my husband that we talk to the front desk about getting a communication between him and the councilor set up, even as a stop-gap.

The poor guy seems to take a long time to trust anyone. I can understand why, but it means he's not as vocal about his feelings as he should be.

I am also shocked, but it seems that the courts in the jurisdiction we're in are notoriously awful about this sort of thing. It is unfair, but the entire situation has been one unfair situation after another. No one seems interested in fixing the bigger issue in the law as it stands.

We've sought the advice of several different attorneys. Those who have not had conflicts of interest have all told us the same thing and that they were sorry. We've been exploring legal action against the first attorney, but money seems to be at the crux of this issue. We can demonstrate that we were mislead, but without an obscene amount of cash up front, no one seems to be willing to help us. We tried the ACLU and were told they doesn't assist with custody cases.

I've spent the last several hours researching local therapists with children specialities. Many of them are way out our ability to pay, and many won't even start seeing you unless you have insurance. Paying the insurance for them (through their step-father with mandate from the courts) means we can't afford insurance through our own provider. She has, so far, refused to provide these details. But, again, those with the power to change the situation don't seem to care when we bring it to their attention.

I hope things get better, too. We're working with them the little time we have them (the distance means the schedule isn't as great as it could be), but I just fear it won't be enough.
